svg.title: Which tool sees which part of a C-23 session
svg.desc: A session runs through four phases: launch and sign-in by the host, app load until interactive, data requests, and business events. Power Platform admin center Monitor sees phases one to three from the platform side for all users, including startup failures, with time to interactive, app open success rate, session count, data request success rate and latency. Application Insights sees only what happens after the app loads: sessionLoadSummary and networkRequest metrics forwarded by the logger, plus Cedar custom events and exceptions. Browser DevTools sees one reproducible session in full detail: console, network requests filtered by apihub.net and dynamics.com, and performance traces.
svg.text: Session phases
1 Launch + sign-in
host, licence, DLP
2 Load → interactive
bundle, first data
3 Data requests
Dataverse, connectors
4 Business events
plan saved, errors
Admin center Monitor → Power Apps (all users, phases 1–3)
TTI, app open success rate, sessions, data request success + latency.
Sees startup failures. Recommendations need a managed environment.
Application Insights (all users, after load only, phases 2–4)
customEvents: sessionLoadSummary, networkRequest (setConfig logger)
+ cedar.* custom events and exceptions; KQL p75, alerts (lesson 105)
Blind to launch failures; needs connect-src in CSP.
Browser DevTools (one session you can reproduce, every phase in the browser)
Console: CSP violations, [cedar] logs. Network: filter apihub.net / dynamics.com, status, size, timing.
Performance: long tasks and render cost. Sources: breakpoints with source maps in Local Play.
Use it to explain a pattern that Monitor or Application Insights revealed.
